messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High p95 latency detected in eu-inference-pool. Metric spike at 2026-03-15T02:09:03Z. Affected route: /v1/generate (hosted). Severity: P2. Paging oncall. Links: <https://metrics/redwood/eu/p95|eu-p95>, runbook: <https://wiki/runbooks/eu-latency>

sarah (sre): ack -- I'm on it, pulling up recent deploys + queue metrics. seeing a sudden increase in KV cache misses and queue depth around 02:07. No deploy recorded in last 30m.

mike (oncall): taking pager. handing off from incident-bot. i'll join the call in 2 mins. @sarah can you post the suspected scope (customer impact) + quick mitigations?

sarah (sre): preliminary scope: ~18-25% of requests to eu-hosted routes hitting p95 > 900ms, error rate stable. affected customers likely high-concurrency clients and realtime chat flows. suspected cause: cache eviction storms after transient restart on a subset of nodes -> KV warmup.

oliver (eng): adding logs I pulled from node-gpu-12: 
```
[02:06:58] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.72
[02:07:10] scheduler: queue_depth=210
[02:07:28] kernel: exec_latency_p50=120ms p95=980ms
```

oliver (eng): immediate mitigations I can try: 1) scale up eu-inference pool by +2 nodes (hot), 2) enable fallback routing to eu-small-model for non-LLM-critical customers, 3) temporarily increase prefix cache retention. which do we want first?

mike (oncall): execute scale up and fallback in parallel. i'll run the scaling command and trigger fallback routing. Sarah please coordinate cache retention change (prefer safe increment).

sarah (sre): running scale command now: 
```
# scale up pool
redwoodctl scale --region eu --pool inference-hosted --delta 2 --priority hot
```

sarah (sre): scale requested, API returned job id 3456. nodes initializing (ETA ~90s).

mike (oncall): enabling fallback policy for low-tier traffic: 
```
redwoodctl routing update --region eu --route /v1/generate --fallback-model redwood/eu-small-v1 --match "not tier:enterprise"
```

mike (oncall): fallback enabled. routing change propagated to 7/8 proxies. last proxy pending.

sarah (sre): increasing cache retention by 30s on rolling subset to avoid mass evictions: 
```
redwoodctl config set --component kv-cache --region eu --retention +30s --rolling
```

sarah (sre): retention update in progress. observing cache warmup on node-gpu-12 -> miss_rate dropping to 0.18. queue_depth down to 60.

incident-bot: Status update created: https://status.redwood/incident/1769876543 (draft). Current impact: degraded latency for ~20% of requests in EU. Next update scheduled in 15m or on notable change.

rachel (product-ops): Draft status page blurb (suggested):
"We are investigating increased response times for our EU hosted inference service. Impact: some requests may experience higher latency; error rates are unaffected. Engineers are scaling capacity and applying mitigations. We will provide the next update by 02:30 UTC."

jess (customer-success): I can push a short customer notice to affected top customers once we have ETA. Suggest template: 
"Hi <Customer>, we're currently investigating increased latency in our EU inference service that may affect high-concurrency requests. We're scaling capacity and routing lower-priority traffic to a fallback model to reduce impact. We expect recovery within ~15-30 minutes. We'll follow up when service is restored or if the ETA changes. Sorry for the disruption."

mike (oncall): agreed. i'll post the status page draft and mark the incident as "investigating". posting internal comms for account teams: 
```
Internal: EU inference latency spike (P2). Impact: elevated p95 for subset of customers. Mitigation: scaled pool + fallback routing + cache retention. ETA: ~15-30m. Escalation: @oliver for kernel perf; @sarah for infra. Do not commit model rollouts in EU until cleared.
```

sarah (sre): nodes finished init, job 3456 succeeded. seeing sustained p95 drop to ~220ms across region. cache miss stabilized.

oliver (eng): confirmed kernel p95 back to expected levels on node-gpu-12. looks like warmup + extra capacity resolved the backpressure.

mike (oncall): posting customer notification to affected list now. ETA update: recovery observed at 02:18 UTC. I'll update status page to "monitoring".

incident-bot: Status page update: INVESTIGATING -> MONITORING. Recovery observed 02:18 UTC. Link: https://status.redwood/incident/1769876543

jess (customer-success): sent customer notices to 4 customers (top-tier & high-concurrency). copying template used in message. replies: a couple customers ack, one asked if we will provide post-incident report.

rachel (product-ops): good, prepare a short postmortem note and exec summary for customers requesting background. Suggest include: root cause (cache eviction storm + transient node restart), immediate mitigations (scale + fallback + retention), timeline, customer impact (p95 elevated for ~18-25% of requests for ~11 minutes), and remediation actions (safeguards for cache eviction, more aggressive rolling of cache retention, automated fallback thresholds).

mike (oncall): moving to incident wrap-up. tasks: 1) revert fallback routing for normal traffic once confirmed stable (me), 2) open postmortem doc (sarah + oliver), 3) notify customers who asked for report (jess). We'll check back in 1h for follow-up and long-term mitigations.

sarah (sre): fallback routing reverted at 02:45 UTC after monitoring period. system stable. creating postmortem draft now: https://wiki/postmortems/1769876543-draft

oliver (eng): notes added to postmortem with perf traces and command logs.

jess (customer-success): queued customer follow-ups. will bump if any additional asks.

mike (oncall): closing thread. thumbs to team :thumbsup: great coordination. will attach incident timeline to the postmortem and schedule a follow-up retro.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. Final state: MONITORING -> RESOLVED. Duration: 00:36:57 (start 02:09:03, recovery 02:18:00, full revert 02:45:00). Postmortem: https://wiki/postmortems/1769876543-draft
